name: Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE)
intro: 人类的终极考试 (HLE) 是一个多模态基准测试，旨在衡量大型语言模型 (LLM) 在人类知识前沿的能力。该基准包含2500道跨数学、人文和自然科学等数十个科目的问题，由全球主题专家开发。HLE的问题设计独特，具有明确且易于验证的已知答案，但无法通过互联网快速检索。目前最先进的LLM在该基准上表现出较低的准确性和校准度，这突显了当前LLM能力与人类专家水平之间的显著差距。
modality: 文本, 图像, 多模态
intro_en: Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE) is a multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate large language models’ (LLM) capabilities at the frontier of human knowledge. It includes 2,500 questions across dozens of subjects such as mathematics, humanities, and natural sciences, developed by global domain experts. HLE’s questions are uniquely designed with clear, verifiable known answers that cannot be quickly retrieved from the internet. State-of-the-art LLMs currently show low accuracy and calibration on this benchmark, highlighting a significant gap between their abilities and human expert levels.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2501.14249. HLE is a 2,500-question multimodal closed-ended academic benchmark built by nearly 1,000 subject-expert contributors from over 500 institutions in 50 countries. Submissions include question text, answer specification, rationale, subject, and contributor affiliation. Questions are designed to be precise, unambiguous, short-answer or multiple-choice, verifiable, and resistant to quick internet lookup. Each question first undergoes frontier-LLM difficulty checks; roughly 13,000 questions that stumped LLMs moved to expert human review. Reviewers with graduate degrees run two review rounds: iterative feedback with 1-3 reviews, followed by organizer/expert approval. A public review period and community feedback corrected concerns. Evaluation reports accuracy and RMS calibration on closed-ended questions.
